content: I can't believe they let me go like that. It feels like I'm just some number on a spreadsheet now, nothing more. They didn’t care about my work at all, and the way they told me was so cold, like it was no big deal. And now everyone acts like everything is fine, but how could it be? They think they can just pat me on the back and say 'it's going to be okay,' but it’s not that simple. I messed up badly, and now I’m a failure. No one even cares enough to understand what this means for me.

That must feel really tough right now. It sounds like you're dealing with a lot of emotions about how it all happened and how people are reacting. What has been the hardest part for you since finding out?

The hardest part is knowing that they didn't even give me a chance to explain myself or say goodbye properly. They just called me in, told me my project was canceled, and then I was out. It felt like they were getting rid of me as quickly as possible. And now everyone acts like it's no big deal, but every time someone tries to comfort me, I feel more irritated because their words sound so hollow. Like they don't even understand what this means for my life. They think everything is going to be okay, but how can it be when I feel like a failure and nobody cares?

It sounds really tough not having that chance to say goodbye properly and feeling like your colleagues might not fully understand what you’re going through. How are you finding the support—or lack thereof—from friends or family outside of work?

My friends and family mean well, but their attempts at comfort just feel like they're trying to make themselves feel better by telling me it'll all be okay. They don't really get it. I know they care, but every time they say something like 'it's going to be fine,' or 'you’ll find another job soon,' I just want to snap at them. It’s not that simple. How can they understand the depth of this? They think they're helping, but all their words sound so empty and repetitive. And when they keep saying the same things over and over again, it just makes me more frustrated because nothing is going to change with those platitudes.

It sounds like you’re really picking up on the well-meaning but sometimes hollow nature of their support. It can be tough when people try to help but don’t quite hit the mark. Have there been any specific moments where you felt particularly understood or closer to them despite the frustration?

There have been a few moments, but they're rare and fleeting. Once my sister sat with me for hours without saying much, just being there. That was nice because I didn't feel like she was trying to fix everything. But then when she started talking about how it'll all work out eventually, I felt that familiar irritation creeping back in. It’s hard not to snap at her because every time someone tries to offer comfort, they seem to miss the mark. They just don’t get how deeply this has affected me and how much I feel like a failure.

Those moments of quiet presence can be really meaningful. It sounds like your sister cares a lot about you. Maybe there are ways to communicate what would help during these times, so she knows when you need space or just someone to sit with quietly. Have you thought about talking more openly with her about how you feel?

Talking to my sister about it might help, but I doubt it will make much of a difference. Every time I try to explain myself, they act like they understand, but then they go back to saying the same empty things over and over again. It’s frustrating because no matter how many times I tell them what I’m going through, they still miss the mark. They just don’t get it, and every attempt to help feels patronizing. So even if I talk more openly with her, I doubt she’ll really understand. It’s like talking to a wall sometimes.

It can be frustrating when you feel like no matter what you say, people still miss the mark. Sometimes just expressing those feelings directly can make a difference though. Have you considered sharing how it feels in the moment when their words don’t resonate with you? Maybe there’s a way to find that balance where they understand more deeply.

I’ve tried telling them before, but every time I do, they seem to think they get it and then go back to saying the same things. It’s like no matter what I say, they just can’t grasp how deep this hurts. They keep offering the same empty platitudes, and when I point out that their words don’t really help, they either repeat themselves or act like they already know everything. So even if I try again to explain it to my sister, I doubt she’ll get it any better than anyone else has. It’s just going to make me feel more frustrated in the end.

It sounds like you’ve had a lot of those conversations before. Maybe trying a different approach or finding specific moments to share your feelings could help. Have there been times when talking about it felt even slightly better, no matter how small?

There have been a couple of times when talking about it felt slightly better, but only for a moment. Like when I vented to my friend Sarah and she just listened without interrupting or offering quick fixes. It was nice to feel heard, but then as soon as she started suggesting things like 'you’ll find another job' or 'it’s not that bad,' the frustration came back. So even those brief moments of feeling understood are quickly overshadowed by the repetition of empty words. It’s exhausting trying to explain myself over and over again when it feels like no one really gets it.

It sounds like having someone who listens without immediately offering solutions can be quite refreshing. Maybe you could suggest to your sister or others that you just need a space to vent and be heard, without expecting quick fixes. That might help create more of those moments where you feel truly understood.
